source_scope: Only the two generated editorial passes are recovered. No original medical PDF, private raw record, credential or protected closing is included.

pass_two_text_changes.before: I recall the words, “Leave me out of it”; I present that phrase as recollection, not as a verified transcript or an established explanation of motive.
pass_two_text_changes.after: I preserve “Leave me out of it” as my recollection in the August 4 and September 10 letters, not as a verified transcript or a finding of motive. [S26][S27]
pass_two_text_changes.reason: Locate the recollection in the supplied August 4 and September 10 letters; repetition is not corroboration.

pass_two_text_changes.before: The AMA's informed-consent opinion treats consent as a communicative process involving understanding, voluntariness, relevant information, and documentation, with a separately described urgent-treatment exception. [S06]
pass_two_text_changes.after: The AMA's informed-consent opinion describes a process of understanding, voluntary choice, relevant information, and documentation, with a separately described urgent-treatment exception. [S06]
pass_two_text_changes.reason: Preserve the consent-process ethical scope and separate urgent exception.

pass_two_text_changes.before: The current HHS Section 504 web rule specifies WCAG 2.1 compliance dates of May 11, 2027 for recipients with at least fifteen employees and May 10, 2028 for smaller recipients, subject to the rule's terms. [S09]
pass_two_text_changes.after: The current HHS Section 504 web rule specifies WCAG 2.1 Level A and Level AA compliance dates of May 11, 2027 for recipients with at least fifteen employees and May 10, 2028 for smaller recipients, subject to its terms. [S09]
pass_two_text_changes.reason: Specify WCAG Level A/AA and current recipient-size dates without backdating.

pass_two_text_changes.before: When a portal becomes unavailable or unusable for a required exchange, please specify an accessible written alternative, its recipient, and its response expectations.
pass_two_text_changes.after: For a required written exchange, please determine whether MyChart is stable and usable or provide an effective written alternative with an identified recipient and response expectations.
pass_two_text_changes.reason: Do not turn a reported threat to portal access into an established termination.

pass_two_text_changes.before: For the September 9 notice, examine the original wording, supporting incidents and dates, author and approver roles, signature condition, consequences, review route, and the material actually considered before it was issued.
pass_two_text_changes.after: For the September 9 notice, identify its authors and approvers, supporting incidents, materials reviewed, applicable policies, and decision process; distinguish the wording now available from facts that the wording alone cannot establish. [S24]
pass_two_text_changes.reason: The original three-page notice has now been examined; underlying decisions remain unexamined.

pass_two_text_changes.before: My September 17 response states my willingness to comply with legitimate requirements while declining the supplied acknowledgment; it is evidence of my stated position, not independent verification of everything the clinic did. [S02]
pass_two_text_changes.after: My September 17 response affirms willingness to comply with legitimate requirements while declining the supplied acknowledgment; the clinic notice also permits agreement by MyChart message, so a signature-only description would be inaccurate. [S02][S24]
pass_two_text_changes.reason: Retain the express MyChart alternative to a signature without presuming acceptance of qualified assent.

pass_two_text_changes.before: Please identify the actual portal restrictions and available routes instead of relying solely on either party's general characterization of access.
pass_two_text_changes.after: Please identify the actual status of each MyChart function and any restriction, notice, or alternative; neither the clinic's reference to standard channels nor my report of a threatened restriction establishes the entire portal history. [S02][S24]
pass_two_text_changes.reason: Separate multiple standard channels, exclusive MyChart use, and actual restriction states.

pass_two_text_changes.before: HIPAA access and amendment have different procedures: access generally requires action within thirty days, while amendment generally allows sixty days, and each permits one additional extension of up to thirty days with the required timely written explanation. [S10][S11]
pass_two_text_changes.after: HIPAA access generally requires action within thirty days, with one additional extension of up to thirty days accompanied by the required timely written explanation. [S10]
pass_two_text_changes.reason: Split the access clock from the amendment clock now separately tracked as C249.

pass_two_text_changes.before: California Penal Code section 11160 applies to specified practitioners and treatment circumstances involving known or reasonably suspected physical injuries associated with the conduct described in the statute. [S15]
pass_two_text_changes.after: California Penal Code section 11160 addresses qualifying practitioners providing medical services for a physical condition where the specified injury and knowledge or reasonable-suspicion predicates are met. [S15]
pass_two_text_changes.reason: Retain actual practitioner, service, injury and knowledge/suspicion predicates.

pass_two_text_changes.before: For a nonurgent institutional response, I request the thirty-calendar-day period stated in my September 17 submission, measured from actual receipt, while asking that urgent clinical needs and any shorter applicable legal deadlines be handled on their own terms. [S02]
pass_two_text_changes.after: I request the thirty-calendar-day resolution period stated in my September 17 response, measured from actual receipt of that response, subject to urgent clinical needs and any different applicable legal timetable. [S02]
pass_two_text_changes.reason: Keep the patient's receipt-based response request separate from the notice's letter-date condition.
